stops.note: light, not heavy, combined with re- (again)
to lift up again, to lighten, from re- and levis
stops.meaning: to lift up again, to lighten

stops.note: carried into French for lightening a burden or raising something up
stops.meaning: to lighten a burden or raise something up

stops.note: settled as the English word for lessening pain, distress, or a burden
stops.meaning: to lessen pain, distress, or a burden

current_meaning: to lessen pain, distress, or a burden, bringing comfort
